title: WPL Season 5 Auction Set for October 28 in Kochi, BCCI Confirms
excerpt: The Board of Control for Cricket in India announced the fifth edition of the Women's Premier League will run from January 14 to February 7, 2027, with the player auction at the Grand Hyatt Kochi and a September 28 deadline for franchises to submit retention lists.
body:
• The Board of Control for Cricket in India announced the fifth edition of the Women's Premier League will be played from January 14 to February 7, 2027.
  • The player auction will be held on October 28, 2026, at the Grand Hyatt in Kochi — a month after the September 28 deadline for franchises to submit their retention lists.
  • The five franchises can build squads of up to 18 players, including a maximum of six overseas players, under a Rs 15 crore salary cap.
  • Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Mumbai Indians have two titles each; Delhi Capitals have finished runners-up in all four editions so far.

MUMBAI — The Board of Control for Cricket in India has set the calendar for the fifth season of the Women's Premier League, confirming the 2027 edition will run from January 14 to February 7, with the player auction scheduled for October 28, 2026, at the Grand Hyatt in Kochi.

The BCCI informed the five franchises — Mumbai Indians, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Delhi Capitals, Gujarat Giants and UP Warriorz — of the dates on Wednesday. All five must submit their player retention lists by September 28, giving teams a month to lock in core rosters before the Kochi auction, where they will fill the remaining squad slots.

The Auction Mechanics

The October 28 auction follows the 2026 mega auction and operates as a recalibration round: franchises rebuild and rebalance under existing squad rules rather than starting from scratch. Each team can assemble a squad of up to 18 players, including a maximum of six overseas players, and will operate under a Rs 15 crore purse.

The retention deadline is the first inflection point. Decisions made by September 28 will determine how much each franchise has left to spend in Kochi and which holes they need to plug — the balance between batting, bowling and all-round options that separates a complete squad from a top-heavy one.

A League Still Climbing

Since its inaugural edition in 2023, the WPL has grown into one of the most watched women's cricket leagues in the world. Smriti Mandhana-led Royal Challengers Bengaluru are the defending champions, having beaten Delhi Capitals in the 2026 final. Mumbai Indians and RCB have won two titles each; Delhi Capitals, runners-up in every edition so far, remain the league's most frustrated contender.

The 2026 season was played in Navi Mumbai and Baroda, with the final held in Vadodara. For 2027, the BCCI has not yet finalised host venues. Mumbai's Brabourne Stadium and Vadodara's Kotambi Stadium lead the shortlist, with a newly constructed venue in Varanasi also under evaluation — though reports suggest it would first need to prove itself by hosting domestic matches before being trusted with WPL fixtures.

The Diaspora Angle

The WPL's auction pool has always mixed established international stars with young Indian talent, and the six-overseas-players rule keeps the league a genuine global showcase. For the diaspora, that mix is the draw: NRI cricket fans in the US, UK and Australia follow the league closely, and the auction is often the first glimpse of the next season's narratives — which young Indian cricketer the franchises gamble on, and which overseas star anchors each dressing room.

What's Next

All eyes now shift to September 28, when the retention lists land and each franchise's auction purse comes into focus. The BCCI is expected to finalise venues and the detailed schedule in the coming weeks, and the final auction player pool will sharpen the picture of which teams are chasing what in Kochi on October 28.
